metadata.case_name: LUI YEE KWOK AND OTHERS v. YAU TAK SHING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: 3rd year student in the English Department of Baptist College

source: Dr. Michael Lee, a Specialist in Neurology, has seen the plaintiff on no fewer than fifty occasions and describes these symptoms as post-concussional.

He explained this to be a condition whereby the patient suffers genuine attacks such as headaches and nausea which cannot be explained by organic damage but are precipitated by feelings of acute anxiety. In this case he feels the precipitating factors are the loss of a limb and the fact that the plaintiff feels that she is different from other people.
(iii) The right side of the chest was tender with fractures to the right 3rd rib and right acromion process of the scapular bone.

injuries.description: Fracture of the right acromion process of the scapular bone
injuries.body_part: right acromion process of the scapula
source: (iii) The right side of the chest was tender with fractures to the right 3rd rib and right acromion process of the scapular bone.

injuries.description: Right arm and forearm crushed beyond repair; above-elbow amputation
source: The right arm and forearm were crushed beyond repair. An "above-elbow" amputation was carried out.
The above elbow amputation has left a stump measuring 9 inches in length.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation at level between right shoulder and elbow

injuries.description: Compound fracture of the right femur fixed internally with double rush pins
source: (ii) Two wounds 10" and 3" in length were suffered on the right thigh with a compound fracture of the right femur. The wounds were sutured and the fractured femur was fixed internally with double rush pins.
Dr. Wong believes has not united correctly causing an external rotation deformity to the hip joint and restricted flexion movement of the knee.

injuries.description: Fracture of the lateral malleolus of the left ankle; wound over left ankle
source: (iv) A wound 5" long over the left ankle was sutured and a fracture of the lateral malleolus of the left ankle was immobilised by the application of a short leg plaster.
The fracture which occurred in the left ankle had now united well but the plaintiff still feels considerable pain and the ankle is very weak and prone to give way on walking.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple injuries of ankle or foot

injuries.description: Multiple wounds producing numerous permanent scars all over the body
injuries.body_part: multiple sites (right thigh, lower left leg, shoulders, left arm, lower limbs)
source: In the accident the plaintiff received multiple wounds which have left numerous scars all over her body.

Particularly ugly scarring exists on her right thigh and lower left leg. These are still tender and apt to blister when thick trousers are worn. Further scarring has been reported on her shoulders, left arm and lower limbs. I am advised that these are permanent.

injuries.description: Fibrositic nodules on the right scapular bone due to scarring of muscles (right shoulder injury)
source: Persistent pain was also felt in the right shoulder and Dr. Wong attributes this to fibrositic nodules on the right scapular bone which are a result of scarring of the muscles during injury.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at shoulder or upper arm level

injuries.description: Injury to ligament and cartilage structures causing mild neck and back pain
source: The plaintiff has complained of a mild pain in the neck and after sitting for any lengthy period her back aches. Medical examination revealed that this was due to injury to the ligament and cartilage structures.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine

source: On admission she was found to have a 3 inch laceration on the scalp and swelling and tenderness over the left ankle. The scalp laceration was sutured and the ankle was immobilized with a short leg plaster.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: Fracture of the left tibia bone (left ankle region) (Second Plaintiff)
source: An X-ray of the ankle revealed a fracture of the left tibia bone.

The permanent effects of the ankle injury will be the limitations she will experience in running, walking and standing. She will be unable to wear high-heeled shoes and there is a likelihood of the ankle becoming osteo-arthritic in later life.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

injuries.description: Hematoma on the right cheek and right groin; linear abrasion on right hip (Third Plaintiff)
injuries.body_part: right cheek; right groin; right hip
source: (a) Hematoma on the right cheek 3" in diameter.
(b) Hematoma on the right groin 2" in diameter.
(c) A linear abrasion on his right hip measuring 4" x ¼".

manifestations.description: Unable to read or watch television for longer than 30 minutes without suffering headaches and nausea
Severe headaches three or four times per week accompanied by nausea and often vomiting; attacks last from a few hours to half a day
Lack of concentration; unable to concentrate for longer than 30 minutes without resting
Phantom-limb syndrome with considerable pain particularly at night, disturbing sleep
Stump extremely tender; operational scar at the end of the stump extremely tender and painful to touch
External rotation deformity to the hip joint and restricted flexion movement of the knee
Confines the plaintiff's ability to walk to a substantial degree; weakness of the ankles
Left ankle is weak and prone to give way on walking; considerable pain in ankle
Multiple permanent scars tender and apt to blister when thick trousers are worn
Persistent pain in the right shoulder attributable to fibrositic nodules on the right scapular bone
Fracture of right 3rd rib still causes occasional pain when breathing deeply
Scar at the back of the skull is tender to touch and causes pain if it comes into contact with her comb while she is brushing her hair (Second Plaintiff)
Limitations in running, walking and standing; unable to squat; unable to wear high-heeled shoes; likelihood of osteo-arthritis in later life (Second Plaintiff)
Faint scar on the right hip and occasional tiredness in the lower part of the back (Third Plaintiff)

treatments_received: Resuscitation and treatment in shock on admission to Queen Elizabeth Hospital
Internal fixation of fractured right femur with double rush pins
Prosthesis fitted to right arm (1 January 1974)
Intensive physiotherapy at Margaret Trench Rehabilitation Centre
Wounds sutured and left ankle immobilised with short leg plaster
Transfer to Kowloon Hospital for convalescence
treatments_future: Psychiatric treatment might help (as suggested by Dr. Lee)
Further surgery to refashion the stump may help (noted as possible)

losses.description: Above-elbow amputation of the right arm leaving a 9 inch tender stump, phantom limb pain and limited prosthesis utility
Numerous permanent scars all over the body particularly on the right thigh and lower left leg; scars tender and apt to blister
Confined ability to walk to a substantial degree due to deformity of the right femur and weakness of ankles; left ankle weak and prone to give way

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Unable to concentrate for longer than 30 minutes without resting; continual nausea and dizziness restricted her ability to study
In her present state the plaintiff is unemployable; chance of earning any wage in the future is at best remote
Permanent limitations in running, walking and standing for the second plaintiff; inability to squat and to wear high-heeled shoes (Second Plaintiff)
Faint scar on the right hip of the third plaintiff (Third Plaintiff)
Damages for loss of expectation of life awarded in respect of the deceased: $10,000.00 (merging with Fatal Accidents Ordinance award)

comparable_cases.injury_description: The plaintiff, a female aged 18, was incapacitated as a result of an accident.
Male plaintiff, single and aged 27, received serious injuries which prevented further full-time employment.
39 year old male plaintiff with estimated working life of 20 to 25 years.
